method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a country made up entirely of islands.
questions.scope: Island countries and countries sharing an island count; Australia explicitly counts.

questions.prompt: Name a cooking or food-preparation technique.
questions.scope: Recognized techniques for cooking, preparing, cutting, mixing, baking or preserving food count. Real public verb/noun forms share an answer. An ingredient, utensil, finished dish or desired texture alone is not a technique.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with k-pop music.
Name an optical instrument used to aid vision or examine things.
questions.scope: Real instruments that use light to aid sight, magnify, project, examine or measure an optical image or spectrum count. Acoustic and mass-analysis instruments do not qualify merely because a source groups them near spectrometers.

questions.prompt: Name a move from a Pokémon video game.
questions.scope: Named moves from released Pokémon games count, including Z-Moves, Max Moves and Colosseum/XD Shadow moves. Physical/special implementations of the same named move share one answer. Generic actions and moves from fan games do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a hand tool or utensil used to prepare or serve food.
questions.scope: Kitchen hand tools, utensils, serving implements and nonpowered cookware count. Small measuring tools used in food preparation also count. Large powered appliances and foods do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a type of flower.
questions.scope: Recognized common flower types and flowering plants grown for their blooms count, including named horticultural groups and documented varieties. Materials merely named after flowers, artificial flower products and unrelated decorative objects do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of building or place used for worship.
questions.scope: Types of religious worship building or built shrine count across religions. Individual named landmarks and a minister or deity alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a team from the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, WNBA or MLS.
questions.scope: Past and present teams from those six leagues count; familiar short team names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name a named pasta or noodle dish.
questions.scope: Named dishes and established menu preparations count, including familiar meal names such as spaghetti, udon and soba, filled pastas and gnocchi. A bare unfilled pasta-shape name without a dish or established menu preparation does not count. Plain tteokbokki is a rice-cake dish; rabokki includes noodles.

questions.prompt: Name a real DJ or DJ act, past or present.
questions.scope: Real DJs and billed DJ duos or groups count, including people known for presenting recorded music on radio. Being a singer or producer alone does not make someone a DJ. Fictional story DJs and unrelated musical groups do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a bone or named group of bones in the human skeleton.
questions.scope: Standard named bones, fused bones and familiar bone groups count. Left and right instances are the same answer. Cartilage, joints, muscles and organs are not bones.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can produce its own light.
questions.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional animal character.
questions.scope: Named animal characters from any published story count; real celebrity pets do not.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Dallas Mavericks.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish or preparation in which eggs are a main ingredient.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a real island or archipelago.
questions.scope: Real named islands and archipelagos worldwide count, including islands that share a country name. Continental mainlands are not treated as islands. Fictional islands do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of room or specialized indoor space.
Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name an emote from Fortnite.
questions.scope: Any recorded season or collaboration counts. These are cosmetic names, not Battle Royale weapon names.

questions.prompt: Name a cat breed, including experimental and historical breeds.
Name a song with a person's name in its title.
questions.scope: Released songs count; the name can be a real person or a fictional person.

questions.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a dish made mainly from potatoes.
questions.scope: Named dishes count when potato is a main ingredient rather than a garnish.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a landform, natural feature or kind of landscape.
Name an item or block a furnace recipe can produce in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Give the output, rather than the input, of an ordinary furnace smelting or cooking recipe. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a programming, scripting, query, markup or stylesheet language.
questions.scope: Real current and historical computer languages for programs, scripts, database queries, markup or style sheets count. Named dialects also count. Plain data-file formats, code editors and ordinary spoken languages do not count. Named XML vocabularies and document-markup formats count; an organization, generic data model, element or software platform alone is not a language.

questions.prompt: Name a romance movie.
Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a food that is commonly pickled.
questions.scope: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, meats and seafood with established pickled preparations count. Vinegar and brine are ingredients, not foods being pickled.

questions.prompt: Name a color or a named shade.
questions.scope: Recognized English color names and published named shades count, including named pigments, Crayola colors and standard CSS color keywords. Regional spellings and ordinary synonyms share one answer. Patterns are not a single color. Different standard definitions of the same ordinary name do not create extra answers.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that is active at night.
questions.scope: Normally nocturnal or regularly night-active animals count; occasional unusual behavior does not.

questions.prompt: Name a landlocked country.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a named weapon from a video game.
questions.scope: Unique named weapons and established weapon/item names count across all platforms.

questions.prompt: Name a substance or mixture that is normally liquid at room temperature.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a musical genre or subgenre.
Name an NBA team.
Name a tea brand or tea company.
questions.scope: Real current or historical tea brands, tea companies and tea estates count. A tea variety, drink preparation or generic ingredient is not a company or brand. The inventory includes packaged-tea and ready-to-drink brands; owning a separate brand does not automatically make a generic parent-name guess eligible.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Toy Story franchise.
questions.scope: Named or distinctly identified characters from Toy Story films, shorts, series and the Lightyear spin-off count. Established collective character identities such as the Aliens count. Voice actors, film titles and descriptive organizational headings do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of box or boxed storage container.
questions.scope: Types of physical box, chest, crate and boxed storage container count, including cases with a recognizable box form. Metaphorical boxes and software do not.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of arachnid.
questions.scope: Named arachnid groups, species and recognized common kinds count. Spiders, scorpions, ticks, mites, harvestmen and other arachnid orders are included. Insects, crustaceans and myriapods are outside this question.

questions.prompt: Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a real, named bridge.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Action”.
Name a quarterback who started and won a Super Bowl.
questions.scope: The quarterback must have started a winning Super Bowl, through Super Bowl LX in February 2026. Winning a ring as a backup alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a breakfast cereal, cereal brand or named cereal product.
questions.scope: Named breakfast-cereal kinds, brands and products count, including hot cereals, muesli, granola and historical products. An unrelated food does not count just because its maker also sells cereal.

questions.prompt: Name something that can be controlled with a remote.
questions.scope: A real consumer product type with a handheld or app-based remote qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of heron, egret or bittern.
questions.scope: Established named groups and species in the Ardeidae bird family count, including recently extinct species. Common and scientific names are accepted. Real synonyms share an identity; unrelated birds and objects named after birds do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a scientific discipline or academic field.
questions.scope: Recognized sciences and academic research fields count, including mathematics, social sciences, linguistics, medicine and engineering. Subdisciplines and documented historical names count. A result, isolated technique or pseudoscientific practice is not itself an academic discipline.

questions.prompt: Name a movie involving time travel or a time loop.
questions.scope: Films in which characters travel through time or experience a repeating time loop count, including animated movies and shorts. Ordinary flashbacks, dreams about the past and a futuristic setting alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a playable hero in Dota 2.
questions.scope: The complete official playable hero roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts. Items, cosmetics and non-playable creeps are not heroes.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Lady Gaga.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Lady Gaga count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a country whose national flag contains a star.
questions.scope: A visible star on the official national flag qualifies; tiny stars inside a coat of arms count too.

questions.prompt: Name a type of building.
Name a vegetable or edible plant part commonly cooked as a vegetable.
Name a chemical element used in everyday products.
questions.scope: There must be a documented consumer, industrial or medical use; exact product names are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a type of ball used in a sport, game or athletic training.
questions.scope: Named balls used in sports, games or athletic training count, including particular game-ball designs. Pucks, shuttlecocks and punching bags are not balls.

questions.prompt: Name a mystery TV or streaming show.
Name a Pokémon Ability.
questions.scope: Named passive Pokémon Abilities from the core games and Pokémon Conquest count. Moves, types, held items and generic trainer actions are separate concepts.

questions.prompt: Name a real named reef or atoll.
questions.scope: Real named reefs and atolls count, including coral and rocky reefs. A plain island or river is not automatically a reef or atoll.

questions.prompt: Name a type of chair or stool.
questions.scope: Recognizable chair and seated-stool designs count, past or present. Benches, couches, named individual thrones and the person chairing a meeting do not.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can pollinate flowers.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of lamp or lighting fixture.
questions.scope: Real lamps, lighting fixtures and manufactured light sources count, including candles and historical lighting. Fictional individual lamps, stars and naturally glowing organisms do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of custard or a dessert made with custard.
questions.scope: Named custards and desserts made using custard or custard powder count. A cream-only filling does not qualify merely because it is called cream.

questions.prompt: Name a dance style, traditional dance, or named social dance.
Name a player position in a team sport.
questions.scope: Named playing positions from any established team sport count; shared names are one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a block an Enderman can pick up in Minecraft.
questions.scope: The actual block-pickup rule counts, including flowers. Endermen may pick up only certain blocks even if the player can carry other blocks. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name an art movement or recognized visual-art style.
questions.scope: Recognized visual-art movements, schools and historical styles count, including architectural and moving-image art movements. An individual artist, work, generic medium or music genre alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name an object designed to be inflated.
questions.scope: Common inflatable objects and named inflatable equipment types count, whether filled with air, helium or another gas. Objects merely containing an empty cavity do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a food crop with an edible part that normally grows underground.
questions.scope: Roots, tubers, rhizomes, bulbs, corms and underground fruits count. Named crop kinds and established edible varieties count. A normal above-ground fruit does not count merely because the plant has roots.

questions.prompt: Name a river, lake, sea, ocean, gulf, bay or strait.
Name a named dish cooked or wrapped in plant leaves.
questions.scope: Traditional leaf-wrapped food parcels, dishes cooked between leaves or in leaf-lined containers, and dishes traditionally sold wrapped in leaves count. Food merely set on a leaf plate without leaf cooking or wrapping does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a branch or field of mathematics.
questions.scope: Recognized mathematical branches, subfields and established mathematical research disciplines count. Both pure and applied mathematics count. Individual formulas, symbols, isolated theorems and unrelated school subjects do not by themselves name a branch.

questions.prompt: Name a video game where you can drive a car or kart.
questions.scope: The driving must be part of the unmodded game, not a fan modification.

questions.prompt: Name a type of creature from mythology, folklore, or fantasy.
Name a motorsport or established motor-racing series.
questions.scope: Recognized motor-vehicle competitions and racing series count, including cars, motorcycles, boats, snowmobiles and powered aircraft. Drivers, vehicle manufacturers and unpowered sports do not qualify by themselves.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that lays eggs.
questions.scope: Named animal groups and species qualify; males do not have to lay the eggs themselves.

questions.prompt: Name an everyday object with wheels.
questions.scope: Ordinary objects and vehicles count; named types count without needing a brand.

questions.prompt: Name a musical instrument with a keyboard.
questions.scope: Recognized keyboard-instrument types and documented named keyboard instruments or models count. Keys and buttons form the musical playing interface; having ordinary valves or attaching an external controller does not automatically qualify another instrument.

questions.prompt: Name a named object in our Solar System.
questions.scope: Planets, dwarf planets, moons, named asteroids and named comets count; stars beyond the Sun do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of boat, ship or other watercraft.
questions.scope: Kinds of boat, ship, raft or other vessel designed to travel on water or underwater count, past or present. Individual named vessels, wrecks, ice-only vehicles and descriptors of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a culinary nut or a seed people eat.
questions.scope: Culinary nuts and food seeds count, including grains, pulses, spice seeds and nuts that are not botanical nuts. Traditional foods that require preparation count. A named food seed or nut group counts; a botanical class, tree alone, finished sauce or book title does not.

questions.prompt: Name a current MLB team (2026).
Name a printmaking or printing technique.
questions.scope: Recognized methods of producing printed images or text and artistic printmaking methods count. Named additive manufacturing/3D printing methods also count. A printer brand, image subject or unrelated craft alone is not a technique.

questions.prompt: Name a way to pay for something without physical cash.
questions.scope: Payment methods, payment networks and named payment services count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of mushroom or other fungus.
questions.scope: Recognized named fungi, mushroom kinds, molds, mildews and yeasts count. Common or scientific names are accepted. Bacteria, viruses and modern non-fungal slime/water molds do not count; diseases alone are not organism names.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Ed Sheeran.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Ed Sheeran count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Space”.
Name a food commonly served on a stick.
questions.scope: Named foods and established skewer dishes count, including sweets.

questions.prompt: Name a real reservoir or artificial lake.
questions.scope: Named reservoirs and artificial lakes count, including historical and seasonally dry reservoirs. A naturally formed lake does not automatically become a reservoir just because it has a regulated outlet.

questions.prompt: Name a heist movie.
questions.scope: Films built around a robbery, theft, con or organized caper count, including comedies, animated movies and shorts. Television series, directors and a film with only an unrelated passing theft do not automatically count.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the San Antonio Spurs.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. Dallas Chaparrals and Texas Chaparrals ABA seasons also count.

questions.prompt: Name an item used for sewing or mending clothes.
questions.scope: Hand-sewing, machine-sewing and dressmaking tools and supplies count. A finished garment alone is not sewing equipment.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with pop music.
Name a bird that cannot normally fly, including extinct flightless birds.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an invention, tool or piece of technology.
